item.title: DSA co-chair mocked for proudly confirming socialists want to abolish the Senate, national borders, prisons
item.description: DSA co-chair confirmed abolishing the Senate, prisons, borders, and ICE on live TV, sparking fierce backlash from Mike Johnson, Ted Cruz and more.
item.content:encoded:
The national co-chair for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) was mocked by conservatives on Sunday after she proudly confirmed many of the DSA's policy ideas, including abolishing the Senate, eliminating prisons and getting rid of national borders, among others.

Speaking to Fox News' Shannon Bream, Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) national co-chair Megan Romer fired off a series of "yes" and "true" responses when asked whether the organization's platform calls for dismantling major American institutions.

"[You're advocating for] abolish[ing] the Senate?" Bream asked.

"True," Romer responded.

Romer also affirmed the organization's support for replacing the presidency and Supreme Court, abolishing ICE, eventually eliminating national borders while granting amnesty to people living in the country illegally, defunding the Pentagon, phasing out prisons and shifting most large corporations to public ownership.

She said some proposals, including abolishing borders and prisons, are part of the organization's long-term vision.

WATCH: HOUSE DEMS DODGE QUESTIONS ON SOCIALIST AGENDA THAT THREATENS TO ABOLISH KEY INSTITUTIONS

Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, wrote, "These people are insane."

GOP House Speaker Mike Johnson said in a post of the exchange on Fox News, "Read their platform: Abolish the Senate, the Presidency, the Supreme Court and immigration enforcement. Open the border wide. Grant mass amnesty. Defund the Pentagon. The barbarians are inside the gate—and Democrats are WELCOMING them in! Communism is no longer a far-fetched threat. It is here on our SHORES! This isn’t just Common Sense vs. Crazy anymore. It’s Common Sense vs. COMMUNISM."

Actress Patricia Heaton wrote, "Yikes."

DSA MEMBER LEADS DEM PRIMARY IN MIDWEST BATTLEGROUND BUT TRAILS LIKELY GOP NOMINEE: POLL

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., wrote, "The DSA isn’t just gaining influence in New York or California. Bernie Sanders- and Mamdani-backed candidates are winning races across the country. Watch this clip closely. These ideas could be coming to your community sooner than you think."

Rep. Burgess Owens, R-Utah, said in response, "Love that today’s Marxist[s] are so ‘in your face’ honest. This proves the ole saying… ignorance is Bliss."

Tom Tiffany, a Republican running for governor in Wisconsin, said the remarks from Romer sounded like democratic socialist Francesca Hong, who is running in the state's Democratic gubernatorial primary.

"This sounds a lot like DSA-backed @FrancescaHongWI. Does she want to abolish the police? Yep. Does she want to abolish prisons? Absolutely. Did she call for abolishing the U.S. Senate? Yes. Socialism is knocking on Wisconsin’s door. This November, we slam it shut," Tiffany wrote.

When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Hong rejected Tiffany's accusations.

"Tom Tiffany is once again telling lies and inventing quotes, because he can't run on his record. Rep. Hong has never called for abolishing the U.S. Senate. Tiffany cannot produce a single statement where she did, because it doesn't exist. She has spoken about police and prison abolition in the past as an aspirational goal, but it is not her current position, and it's not something she will pursue as governor. She does not support replacing the presidency with the Supreme Court. Eliminating national borders isn't her position either, and it's not even part of the official DSA platform. DSA is a membership organization, not a political party. Rep. Hong is not endorsed by DSA national, and doesn't agree with everything in its national program," Hong communications director Allison Geyer told Fox News Digital.

Hong's campaign website lists the Milwaukee, Northeast Wisconsin and Madison DSA chapters on her endorsement page.

Hong previously appeared on far-left streamer Hasan Piker's show and distanced herself from the streamer during an MS NOW interview in early July.

"I condemn hatred, discrimination, antisemitism and Islamophobia, any sort of dehumanizing of communities," Hong said during the interview. "Being on these streams, it’s important that we get our message out in places where, you know, campaigns struggle to reach voters. Just because I am on a platform certainly does not mean that I endorse everything that has been said by either the hosts or other people who have gone on."

Joe Mitchell, a Republican running for Congress in Iowa, accused Lindsay James, a Democrat running for the same seat, of standing for the same policy positions.

".@Lindsay4Iowa stands for all of this," he wrote.

"No, Lindsay does not support any of these out of touch, ridiculous, policies. Lobbyist Joe Mitchell is lying about Lindsay again because Joe knows his record of enriching himself at Iowans' expense is disqualifying," Jackson Smith, a spokesperson for James' campaign, told Fox News Digital when reached for comment.

The Virginia GOP also demanded all Democrats be asked if they support the policies put forth by the DSA.

"This is what Virginia Democrats think belongs under their 'big tent.' Every Democrat should be asked to explicitly denounce these insane anti-American positions & the DSA. If they refuse to do so, we know where they stand," they wrote on X.

GOP Tennessee Rep. Chuck Fleischmann wrote in response to Romer's statements, "The DSA is a complete inversion of what America stands for; you can watch it for yourself. Their movement is a coordinated effort to undermine our nation’s values and dismantle the freedoms we hold dear. If we don’t stand up, speak out, and defend our country’s core values, we could soon find ourselves watching the America we love slip away."

Pennsylvania Democratic Sen. John Fetterman also called out Romer's comments on X.

He wrote, "This isn’t a big tent—it’s anarchy. Why can’t Dems call out the DSA?"

"This is insane. How can anyone vote for a @DemSocialists member unless you are an anarchist?" Bill Ackman asked on X.

Ackman has been outspoken about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's democratic socialist vision for the Big Apple.

He called his policies a "disaster" for the city, and said he wasn't a fan of the mayor.

The DSA did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Socialist platforms and campaigns are on the rise across the country, including in New York, where two House candidates backed by Mamdani defeated incumbent progressive lawmakers and will likely sail to victory in the November general election. 

A third open House race saw a Mamdani-backed candidate defeat an establishment-backed Democrat.

Fox News' Taylor Penley contributed to this report.

item.title: Why Trump is suddenly threatening Iran's last untouched nuclear site
item.description: Trump threatens to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility, but military experts disagree over whether bunker busters can reach its chambers.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is threatening to strike Iran’s deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility — a site the United States previously left untouched while bombing the country’s other major nuclear sites, raising new questions about what may have changed.

Estimated to lie beneath at least 100 meters of rock near Iran's damaged Natanz nuclear enrichment complex, Pickaxe was designed to replace an above-ground plant capable of assembling roughly 6,000 advanced centrifuges each year before it was destroyed in 2020.

Iran said the replacement would be larger, more modern and built "in the heart of the mountain." Analysts believe the tunnels could eventually hold a centrifuge assembly line, an enrichment plant or equipment used in certain nuclear weaponization activities.

I'VE STUDIED MILITARY STRATEGY. TRUMP NOW FACES IRAN'S OLDEST BATTLEFIELD TRICK

Yet the administration has not said whether it has confirmed that centrifuges were moved inside — or why a site left untouched during earlier attacks now warrants a strike. Military experts also disagree over whether airstrikes could destroy Pickaxe’s interior or merely seal its entrances temporarily.

The same depth that could protect Iran’s nuclear infrastructure may place Pickaxe’s main chambers beyond the reliable destructive reach of America’s most powerful conventional bunker-busting weapon. Bombing its exposed entrances could deny Iran access without destroying the facility or anything stored inside.

Trump said Tuesday that the United States would probably strike the area "pretty soon" and "very heavily."

TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS

His warning came after The Wall Street Journal reported that Israeli intelligence believes Iran moved thousands of centrifuges into Pickaxe last fall. Trump said the transfer "may have" occurred but added that the United States did not have it "on record."

"Maybe this one they have right," Trump said. "But it’s okay. It doesn’t mean anything unless they have the material."

"We follow the material," he added.

TRUMP SEEKS $672M TO STOP IRANIAN NUKES AS NEGOTIATORS WEIGH FATE OF URANIUM STOCKPILE

By "the material," Trump was referring to Iran’s enriched uranium, including uranium gas that centrifuges can further enrich to weapons-grade levels.

Before the June 2025 attacks, the International Atomic Energy Agency had verified that Iran possessed 440.9 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, enough, if further enriched, for approximately 10 nuclear weapons under the agency’s standard measurement.

Most of the stockpile was believed to have been held at Isfahan, with additional material at Natanz and Fordow. Inspectors have since been unable to verify its amount, condition or present location.

The Institute for Science and International Security assesses that the material remains trapped at those three sites and does not believe enriched uranium has entered Pickaxe.

The administration has not said whether the United States independently corroborated the reported Israeli assessment, whether centrifuges are being stored or installed inside Pickaxe or whether nuclear material has entered the facility.

Storing centrifuges would not make Pickaxe an operational enrichment plant. The machines would have to be installed in connected cascades, linked to electrical, ventilation and piping systems and fed uranium gas.

Satellite imagery shows continued construction but no indication that Pickaxe is operational, according to the Washington-based institute. Images from February showed Iran adding concrete, rock and reinforced structures over tunnel portals in an apparent effort to harden them against airstrikes.

Analysts also observed smaller closed-roof vehicles near the entrances that could indicate Iran was outfitting the interior. The imagery could not establish what the vehicles carried.

Spencer Faragasso, a senior research fellow at the Institute for Science and International Security, said earlier U.S. and Israeli attacks prioritized Iran’s operating enrichment program. Based on what was understood about Pickaxe at the time, he said, there was "nothing of priority" inside that warranted expending valuable deep-penetrating weapons.

"The facility is still under construction, and it’s unlikely that a centrifuge plant is operating inside there," Faragasso told Fox News Digital.

But Faragasso said centrifuges could have entered aboard covered trucks without being detected in commercial imagery, making the reported Israeli intelligence plausible but impossible for outside analysts to confirm.

The reported transfer could help explain Trump’s recent focus on Pickaxe, he said. The facility is also one of the last nuclear-related sites of its size that has not been struck.

Trump did not publicly name Pickaxe during the opening months of Operation Epic Fury. It entered his public rhetoric July 13, when conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt raised the facility during an interview.

Trump said American surveillance had detected no activity there but called Pickaxe a possible target for a "nice big fat shot right into the front door."

At the end of the interview, Hewitt urged Trump to "go get Pickaxe Mountain."

"We’re going to take out Pickaxe Mountain," Trump replied. "Tell the Iranians to be ready."

The White House could not be reached for comment for this story.

The administration has not explained whether the recent threats reflect new intelligence, an effort to deter Iran from activating the facility or a shift from destroying existing enrichment capacity to preventing Iran from rebuilding.

Whether the United States could destroy Pickaxe from the air remains disputed.

Nicole Grajewski, an assistant professor at Sciences Po and nonresident scholar in the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace’s Nuclear Policy Program, said it would be "very close to impossible" to destroy the facility through an air campaign like the one the United States carried out against Fordow.

Pickaxe is deeper and more heavily fortified, she said, and does not have a publicly confirmed structural weakness comparable to those exploited there.

Retired Air Force Brig. Gen. Robert Spalding, a former B-2 operations commander, said planners would first determine whether the mission required destroying Pickaxe’s interior or merely preventing Iran from using it.

"You assess what the goals are, and then you assess the costs associated with making something not fit for use — or destruction," Spalding said.

If destroying the facility proved infeasible, he said, the U.S. could instead deny access and prevent Iran from bringing in the personnel and equipment needed to operate it.

The institute has identified two possible ventilation-shaft locations through satellite imagery, including one it considers probable. Without internal schematics, however, analysts cannot confirm their purpose or connection to the main chambers.

Faragasso said the shafts could provide weak points for deep-penetrating weapons, although the results of an attack might remain unclear.

"The facility is not invulnerable," he said. "There are options."

"At the minimum, the tunnel entrances can be collapsed," Faragasso added, saying a strike could also send damaging shock waves into the facility.

Grajewski said collapsing the portals would prevent Iran from moving personnel or equipment in or out without first undertaking an excavation visible to American and Israeli surveillance. Any effort to reopen Pickaxe could trigger another strike.

But Iran has previously excavated entrances to missile tunnels after they were attacked, meaning keeping Pickaxe closed could require continued surveillance and repeated military action.

Grajewski said a strike could provide the U.S. with a "symbolic win" against one of Iran’s most prominent remaining nuclear-related facilities but would not eliminate the broader program.

"It is a very high-value facility," she said. "But it’s not the entirety of the Iranian nuclear program."

item.title: 'Shame on you': Sherrill knew voter-roll bombshell was coming when she called Trump a liar, DOJ official says
item.description: Harmeet Dhillon says Gov. Mikie Sherrill knew about New Jersey's voter roll bombshell before she accused Trump of lying about noncitizen voting.
item.content:encoded:
The Justice Department's top Civil Rights official accused New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill of criticizing President Donald Trump's election integrity claims even though she already knew her administration was about to disclose a major voter registration problem.

In his July 16 address, Trump accused China of acquiring sensitive voter data and said U.S. intelligence agencies hid that revelation from the public while also alleging several Democrat-run states, including New Jersey, have large numbers of noncitizens registered to vote.

Department of Homeland Security data released in concert with the speech found more than 35,000 potential noncitizens are on the Garden State’s rolls.

"When the president came out with his Primetime speech last Thursday, I believe in the sequencing of events that has been laid out, she already knew that this revelation was forthcoming," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon said.

'SHADOW GOVERNMENT': TRUMP CLAIMS INTEL COMMUNITY BRAGGED ABOUT HIDING CHINESE MEDDLING

"She knew it, and she still went online and called the president a liar and said he was exaggerating -- Shame on you, governor."

Dhillon said governors willing to cooperate with the DOJ would receive assistance but warned states refusing to do so could face lawsuits.

"It's a bipartisan problem, actually. And I'm really looking forward to helping everyone who will work with us fix this problem. And if they won't work with, we'll sue them and we'll still fix the problem."

Following Trump’s address, Sherrill signed on to a statement with 23 other Democratic governors attempting to throw cold water on the president's wide-ranging claims, calling him a liar, as Dhillon said.

"It's deeply alarming that President Trump continues to try to undermine free and fair elections. No amount of lies and conspiracy theories can change the fact that our country's elections have repeatedly been proven to be safe and secure," read the rebuke, formally led by Kentucky Gov. Andrew Beshear.

TONY DOKOUPIL CLASHES WITH MARK WARNER AFTER THE SENATOR RIPPED CBS FOR AIRING TRUMP SPEECH ‘AS NEWS’

Sherrill’s co-signed statement went on to accuse Trump of trying to "intimidate and silence voters" while claiming Democrats are the ones "actually making life better for American families by lowering costs, creating jobs and protecting our freedoms."

"Ours is a winning message, which is why he is trying to undermine democracy."

Dhillon said Sherrill and all other governors should join with DOJ to investigate every substantive claim of election integrity violations, warning it is their own citizens who stand to be hurt.

"Every single person who voted illegally canceled out the vote of a New Jersey voter; that is shameful," she said.

"And instead of pointing fingers at the president, which is what Governor Sherrill did… she should be raising her hand to work with the federal government to clean this up ASAP because that's the vow she took when she ran for office and she got sworn in as the governor of her state is to protect her citizens, and her citizens have a right to vote."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Dhillon's letter gave Sherrill five business days, expiring Tuesday, to turn over voter data in the case. Meanwhile, Sherrill indicated to WCBS that she wouldn't be complying.

"It is not a surprise ... the Trump administration wants to immediately weaponize this against people as opposed to focusing on making sure we're running free and fair elections," the Democrat said.

Asked about the accusation Sherrill knew about her own state’s motor-voter scandal when she accused Trump of being a liar, Sherrill spokesman Sean Higgins pointed Fox News Digital to comments she made after touring a grocery store in Essex County to sign unrelated legislation.

NEW JERSEY REMOVES 6,600 PEOPLE FROM VOTER ROLLS WHO WERE ELIGIBLE TO CAST A BALLOT FOR 2024 ELECTION

In response to a reporter's question on the scandal, Sherrill said her administration is moving quickly because Jerseyans deserve transparency.

"We're running an independent investigation right now to get to the bottom of exactly how this happened and what's going on, but it is not a surprise to me that the federal government that the Trump administration wants to immediately weaponize this against people as opposed to focusing on making sure that we're running free and fair elections," Sherrill said.

Pennsylvania, New York and several other states have also resisted DOJ requests for voter registration data, arguing federal law and state privacy protections limit what information can be shared.

The DOJ has also sued officials in some of the states over the election integrity crisis, including New Jersey Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell.

item.title: Shark Week dangers hit home as man is badly bitten while saving pregnant fiancée from harm
item.description: Shark attack survivor Jacorey High says he fought off a 4-foot shark in Daytona Beach Shores while rushing his pregnant fiancée to safety. He is speaking out as he recovers.
item.content:encoded:
A Georgia man in his early 20s is recovering after experiencing a shark bite while protecting his pregnant fiancée at a Florida beach.

The man was wading in waist-deep water near the Dunlawton Beach Approach in Daytona Beach Shores shortly before 5:30 p.m. on Saturday — just hours before this year's Shark Week kicked off — when a shark estimated to be about 4 feet long bit his left foot and ankle, Volusia County Beach Safety officials told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"He was treated on scene by Beach Safety personnel and transported to a nearby hospital with non-life-threatening injuries," officials said.

SHARK SIGHTINGS SPIKE NEAR AMERICA'S BEACHES AS JULY 4 CROWDS HEAD TO SHORE FOR WEEKEND

The victim was identified by FOX 5 Atlanta as Jacorey High of Henry County, Georgia. High said his first priority was getting his pregnant fiancée safely out of the water.

"I realized right away it was a shark because of the way it bit down on my foot, but I was more worried about getting my fiancée out of the water," High told FOX 5 Atlanta.

High said the shark continued to pursue him as he tried to escape.

"Then it came up to try to get my arm. So I had to push it away from me. I ran, and it tried to get my other leg," he told the station.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

He described the shark as gray on top and about as tall as the distance from his waist to his feet, according to FOX 5 Atlanta.

After reaching the shore, High realized the severity of his injuries.

"I didn't really feel it until I got to the hospital, when they started giving me medicine for it," he said.

Doctors performed surgery on High's foot after the attack, and he told the station he expects his recovery could take about three months.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"Hoping that it didn't really mess up anything important in my foot so that I can go back to work," High said.

Fox News Digital previously reported that shark experts have urged beachgoers to stay alert this summer as sightings have increased along several U.S. coastlines.

Marine biologist Mike Heithaus of Florida International University told Fox News Digital that shark bites remain unusual, even during the busy summer beach season.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"People should always be aware of local conditions and listen to lifeguards, but shark bites are very rare," he emphasized.

He recommended that people avoid murky water, that they stay away from areas where large schools of fish are visible and that they avoid places where other people are actively fishing.

Fox News Digital reached out to High for further comment about what happened. 

Shark Week 2026 runs from July 26 to Aug. 1 on the Discovery Channel.

item.title: If you want to own a College Basketball team, UNLV is up for sale in wild, but smart, $10 million proposition
item.description: Josh Pastner is offering ownership of the UNLV Runnin' Rebels for $10 to $12 million, a fraction of what a Las Vegas NBA franchise would cost.
item.content:encoded:
Forget about owning an NBA team in Las Vegas, just buy the UNLV basketball team.

No, you aren’t reading that wrong. A college hoops team has decided to lean into this era of NIL and revenue-sharing by putting its squad up for sale, at least according to UNLV head coach Josh Pastner and the athletic department.

In a world that is already filled with college boosters helping pay the steep salaries that come with transfer portal players or high school athletes, UNLV is just saying the quiet part out loud when it comes to purchasing an entire team.

Another crisis for Bill Belichick: UNC places GM Michael Lombardi on administrative leave amid investigation

For years, there have been Las Vegas entrepreneurs hoping to bring a team to Las Vegas, in hopes of joining the other professional leagues that have found a home in 'Sin City'.

But, Josh Pastner is hoping someone will bite on his proposition to ditch the NBA aspirations and put a fraction of that potential costs into college hoops.

CLOCK IS TICKING AS SENATORS TED CRUZ, MARIA CANTWELL PUSH FOR SEC, BIG TEN BUY-IN ON COLLEGE SPORTS BILL

"Buy the college basketball team. It’s legal now. You can be the owner of the UNLV Runnin’ Rebels men’s basketball team, and it’s a lot less expensive," Josh Pastner told Taylor Rocha. "You don’t have to spend over a billion dollars to own our team. I’m asking for $10 to $12 million to own our team, and you still get a great tax write-off. You can be as involved, and you can tell people you are the owner of the team."

No, he's not kidding, and I can't say I blame him for trying.

In fact, UNLV basketball put together graphics on what you could buy with $10 million, compared to owning your own college program.

Running out of time: SEC, Big Ten wait on 'Protect College Sports Act' revisions as August recess nears

"The UNLV Runnin' Rebels are one of the most iconic brands in college basketball. A program with a national championship, final four legacy, and a home in the fastest growing sports city in America," UNLV said in a graphic.

"With Las Vegas hosting NBA Summer League, the 2028 Final Four, and an NBA franchise on the horizon, the Rebels sit at the center of it all. And according to head coach Josh Pastner, for 10 to 12 million dollars, it can all be yours."

I mean, this might be enticing for someone.

Why not?

There are boosters across the country that are hitting the golf course or college tailgate with the main mission of letting anyone who will listen how much money they donated to the program in order to help purchase a player for the team.

I promise, it's happening somewhere as we speak. The only thing missing is a player/owner, like 'Jackie Moon' from the Flint Tropics. If you don't understand the reference, please take the time to look it up, I promise it's worth your time.

For college athletics, the return on investment is hard to justify for any donor. Besides their favorite team cutting down the nets, or hoisting a trophy at seasons end, there really is no true ROI for these boosters.

Sure, third party collectives have gotten creative in offering up a piece of the company to receive dividends on future income that is created by the athletes they invest in. But, being able to call up the university booster with large pockets that is looking to see their team succeed is also based off ego.

For UNLV, the school is offering a chance to own the team, and I still don't know exactly what that looks like if we're being honest.

Obviously, we're talking about courtside seats to the game, or sitting in the luxury box. But, I don't imagine a college basketball coach is wanting to take input on team strategy from someone who is writing the check.

I don't suspect Josh Pastner is going to really want the 'team owner' in the locker room at halftime complaining about the lack of offense from the shooting guards who were paid a large sum of money to produce points.

But, in terms of raising money to compete in the very expensive college basketball world, you have to start somewhere.

item.title: KASH PATEL: Global partners are joining Trump's FBI to take down scam empires for good
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel details how Operation Sand Dollar, Operation Zephyr Exodus, and global law enforcement partners are dismantling scam centers.
item.content:encoded:
The FBI has launched a historic effort to eliminate global scam center fraud that steal Americans’ life savings and fuel some of the world’s most vicious criminal networks. These scam centers are industrial-scale compounds located in cross-border regions on the other side of the world that are run by transnational criminal syndicates that torture workers, steal and launder billions and target Americans and our allies alike. It is a massive, highly sophisticated web of criminality.

Thanks to President Donald Trump’s decisive leadership and prioritization of the battle against scam centers, this FBI has taken the lead in the fight — treating scam centers as a top priority threat to our public and a crucial part of our no-fail mission to crush violent crime and defend the homeland.

Fifteen months ago, we laid out a playbook to dismantle the problem. We went to the source and launched an initiative in Southeast Asia, working with partners in India, Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, and more to scuttle compounds and disrupt their communications capabilities. We joined our private sector technology and financial industry partners to trace infrastructure, seize malicious domains, follow the money, and hunt down the funding streams for their leadership. We launched sweeping ops like Operation Blackout to identify, locate, and annihilate the largest international scam compounds in the region.

In just over a year, this playbook has delivered historic results.

WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

In April, working side-by-side with Dubai Police and China’s Ministry of Public Security, the FBI led Operation Sand Dollar — the largest scam center takedown in our history. We hit nine scam centers run by Asian organized crime actors, made 311 arrests, and seized thousands of devices that had been used to target Americans in the United Arab Emirates. Each of those centers was stealing roughly $6 million a year. Shutting them down meant saving victims $54 million in losses — just from a single operation. 

EXCLUSIVE: FBI ADDS ALLEGED COVID FRAUDSTER ACCUSED OF TAKING $5M FROM KIDS' MEAL PROGRAM TO MOST WANTED LIST

Or look at our work against the Prince Holding Group in Cambodia, a transnational criminal empire running guarded compounds that pumped out global scams. Our takedown, Operation Zephyr Exodus, led to an indictment of their CEO for wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy, and the forfeiture of roughly 127,000 Bitcoin — about $15 billion at the time and the largest forfeiture in U.S. history — ripping out the financial engine of a criminal syndicate that used its ill-gotten gains to attack everyday Americans.

In another operation, we went after the Tai Chang scam compound in Burma, operated by Chinese criminals. We seized domains and $30 million tied to this and other compounds. One more op — a joint effort between the FBI’s Bangkok office and our Thai partners — took down the Shunda compound, linked to hundreds of millions in losses. They’d used a Telegram channel with over 6,000 followers to recruit forced labor into a Cambodian law enforcement impersonation scam — and we seized it.

We are not just reacting after the damage is done. Through Operation Level Up, an FBI initiative supported by the U.S. Secret Service and other partners, we are proactively identifying potential victims in real time. So far, we have notified nearly 9,000 people, about three-quarters of whom did not know they were being scammed. We have prevented an estimated $562 million in losses and referred dozens of people for suicide intervention. That’s what it means to treat this as a no-fail mission.

FBI BOSS KASH PATEL DETAILS HOW AGENCY AND PARTNERS SECURED RECORD-SHATTERING FIFA WORLD CUP

The scale of our global offensive against scam centers is unprecedented. We’ve now opened more than 30 FBI cases, pursued or helped restrain assets valued at more than $15 billion, and helped drive hundreds of arrests. We’ve suspended more than 7,500 terminals, cutting off the internet lifeline that powers thousands of scam devices at a time — thanks to this FBI’s tremendous partnership with the private sector. And just this past week, we hosted the FBI’s first-ever Scam Center Summit in Thailand – bringing together partners from 18 countries and hundreds of law enforcement agencies, igniting our mission to ensure scam centers can never again take a foothold in the region.

Through these actions, we haven’t just protected Americans; we’ve freed thousands of trafficking victims from forced-labor compounds. And we’re just getting started.

None of this is possible if we work alone. defend the homeland from global scam centers, we rely on ironclad partnerships, with the Royal Thai Police, Dubai Police, China’s Ministry of Public Security, Cambodian National Police, Indonesian National Police, and India’s Central Bureau of Investigation, to name a few our allies across Southeast Asia. When we combine our world-class intelligence capabilities, overseas law enforcement access, sanctions, and cutting-edge technology, these criminals have nowhere to hide.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

What’s next? At our Scam Center Summit, I informed our partners we would be bulldozing these compounds to show the world what full mission success is and challenged them to be the first to participate in this historic effort. We will also continue to target every level of syndicate leadership to ensure total dismantlement of these organizations is achieved. Action is what matters, and it is what this FBI will continue to deliver thanks to the Trump administration.

This FBI will keep driving forward and dismantle compounds, seize billions, rescue trafficking victims, return people’s life savings, and rubble these networks. They may think they can target Americans from safe havens overseas. Perhaps they should read the above.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie delivers 'very specific' message to mom's kidnapper 25 weeks after her abduction
item.description: Savannah Guthrie posted an emotional Instagram plea with a "very specific" message directed at whoever kidnapped her mother, Nancy Guthrie.
item.content:encoded:
Savannah Guthrie delivered a "very specific" message to her mother's kidnapper on Monday, more than 25 weeks after the 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie vanished from her Arizona home.

In an emotional plea posted to her Instagram account, Savannah Guthrie appealed directly to whoever is responsible for the kidnapping, saying that her family is "in agony" and "will never stop looking for her."

"Do the right thing now," Guthrie urged her mother's unidentified kidnappers. "Make the right choice. Help us find her. Tell us where to look for her." 

NANCY GUTHRIE UPDATE: 25 WEEKS AFTER ABDUCTION, ELIZABETH SMART SAYS THERE'S ‘REASON TO HAVE HOPE’

"I'm coming on today with a very specific message. It has been months since our mom was taken from us. Our family is in agony. We are in a nightmare that will not end. Nothing about our situation has changed. We have done our part, and we will never stop looking for her. We will always ache for her and feel that hole in our hearts. The world can be a cruel and unforgiving place," Savannah Guthrie said.

"I truly believe it is never too late to do right thing. Help us bring this situation to an end. For all of us. No matter where we've been and what we've done, I believe there is always a way home. Please make the right choice."

item.title: German officials want to know why Berlin attack suspect was free despite alleged ISIS support
item.description: German officials are left to scrutinize why the suspect in a violent attack in Germany was roaming the streets despite alleged ISIS sympathies.
item.content:encoded:
In the wake of the recent violent attack in Berlin near a pride festival, German officials are left to contend with the questions surrounding why suspect Abdul Ballout was free to perpetrate the assault despite his recent conviction related to supporting ISIS.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Monday wished to know how the violent assault could have been prevented.

"We must do everything to protect people in Germany as best possible from such criminals, from dangerous people who for whatever reason can’t be taken into custody," Merz said, according to The Associated Press.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told public broadcaster ZDF during an interview that in light of the 21-year-old suspect's conviction and record of backing the Islamic State, it did not make sense that the man was roaming free.

"You can assume that it certainly would have made sense to put this person in custody," he noted, according to the report.

BERLIN PRIDE ATTACK SUSPECT KILLED IN POLICE CONFRONTATION: AP

Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner told regional broadcaster RBB in an interview that while he did not wish to question the independence of the court system, when it comes to the matter of this attack, "words fail me."

The suspect in the recent Berlin attack went to Lebanon last year with the goal of traveling to Syria to join ISIS, according to an English translation of a joint release from the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office and the Berlin Court of Appeal, which noted that the man "was born and raised in Berlin and is a German citizen."

The attack on Saturday night left one dead and 29 injured, according to the AP, which reported that 21-year-old Abdul Ballout is suspected of plowing a van into people near a pride festival prior to apparently slashing people with a machete in what authorities think was a terror attack.

The suspect was killed by authorities on Sunday.

"According to current information, the 21-year-old allegedly attacked the special forces officers with a bladed weapon, whereupon they used their firearms," an English translation of a July 26 joint press release from the Berlin Police and public prosecutor's office noted. "The man suffered fatal injuries and died at the scene. The investigation is ongoing."

ISIS POISED TO EXPLOIT HISTORIC US IRAQ EXIT, TERROR GROUP 'ACTIVELY WAITING IN THE GAPS,' EXPERT WARNS

Earlier this year, a Berlin juvenile court convicted Ballout of preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state, and publishing propaganda supporting ISIS.

A news release from the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office and Berlin Court of Appeal said the court sentenced Ballout to one year and 10 months in youth custody before prosecutors appealed.

Officials have stated that the man was granted a suspended sentence, but the news release states: "The decision regarding the suspension of this sentence on probation was deferred for six months pursuant to Section 57 in conjunction with Section 61 Paragraph 1 of the Juvenile Courts Act. The court also imposed various conditions on Abdul B., including placing him under the supervision of a probation officer. The court lifted the existing arrest warrant, as pretrial detention primarily serves to secure the criminal proceedings and does not constitute a prejudicial punishment."

FBI ARRESTS 3 MEN WHO ALLEGEDLY PLEDGED ALLEGIANCE TO ISIS, FUNDED DRONE ATTACKS TARGETING US TROOPS OVERSEAS

The news release noted that the case was not over, given that the appeals process had yet to play out.

"This conviction is not yet legally binding, as the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office has filed an appeal. The Public Prosecutor's Office had requested a longer, non-probationary sentence for a juvenile and the continuation of the arrest warrant," the release noted.

item.title: Financial hardship may age the brain faster, researchers say in new study
item.description: Chronic poverty over decades was linked to memory loss, slower processing speed and brain shrinkage, with strongest effects among men and APOE-ε4 carriers.
item.content:encoded:
Adults who faced persistent financial hardship showed poorer cognitive performance and signs of accelerated brain aging later in life, according to a new study.

Researchers at University College London looked at 2,759 U.K. participants from the MRC National Survey of Health and Development born in 1946, as stated in a press release.

Adults who reported experiencing persistent financial hardship or low income performed worse on cognitive tests that assessed verbal memory and processing speed.

LONGER LIVES, WORSE HEALTH? SCIENTISTS UNCOVER TROUBLING TREND ACROSS GENERATIONS

Those who had persistent low income also showed poorer brain health based on MRI scans, which measured markers of aging like brain shrinkage and enlarged ventricles.

"[While] we know well that cognitive decline is associated with both genetic risks and adverse childhood experience, we knew very little about what happens during the life course … particularly, the experience of persistent financial stress over the lifetime," study author Dr Jacques Wels from the Unit for Lifelong Health & Ageing at UCL told Fox News Digital.

ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TESTS MAY PREDICT SYMPTOMS YEARS IN ADVANCE, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION

"The study clearly demonstrates … that the accumulation of poverty is linked to cognitive decline. We used different measures of lifecourse financial adversity and different measures of cognitive decline and they all show the same results, which makes the results solid."

The associations were strongest among men, people who had disadvantaged childhoods and carriers of the APOE-ε4 genetic variant that is linked to a higher risk of Alzheimer's disease.

"The study shows that [while] cognitive decline is both a matter of genetic risks and individual behaviors, it is also affected by the experiences we live over our lives that we don’t always have control on," Wels added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Based on the findings, the researchers suggested that chronic financial adversity over decades, rather than short-term periods of hardship, is linked to faster cognitive aging.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

This could be the result of chronic stress leading to inflammation or increased cognitive load from persistent financial worry, the authors proposed.

There were some limitations of the study, including that its observational design could not prove that the financial stress caused the cognitive effects.

"We are looking at a cohort of people born in 1946 – so their life course experience is really dependent on the context they lived in," Wels noted. "For instance, we found stronger effects among males, which reflects the ‘breadwinner’ role of men in older cohorts, something we might not observe in more recent generations."

Even after accounting for many other factors that could influence brain health, it's still possible that unmeasured variables may have affected the results, the study authors acknowledged.

While reducing long-term poverty could help protect brain health, the UCL team said further studies are needed to determine whether improving financial circumstances directly reduces the risk of cognitive decline and dementia.

item.title: Cracker Barrel CEO out on heels of failed rebrand that removed Uncle Herschel logo, infuriated customers
item.description: Julie Masino exits as Cracker Barrel CEO after the failed logo change and rebrand that removed Uncle Herschel sparked accusations of going "woke."
item.content:encoded:
Cracker Barrel announced on Monday that CEO Julie Masino will step down roughly one year after a disastrous attempt to modernize the company infuriated customers and forced a stunning about-face. 

Last summer, the Cracker Barrel restaurant chain famously changed its logo and store interiors while removing the "Old Timer" dubbed "Uncle Herschel" from its branding. The rebrand was part of a $700 million overhaul across the company's 660-plus restaurants, which also included a revamped menu. 

Uncle Herschel, who depicted a traditional Southern general store personality, was replaced by a minimalist redesign that dropped the character. The chain’s iconic decorative knickknacks were also scaled down. 

But the changes didn’t go over well, and the brand was vilified on social media, with longtime customers arguing the company was abandoning the nostalgic look that had defined the brand for decades. Conservatives accused the restaurant chain of going "woke," and many longtime customers insisted they wouldn’t return. 

CRACKER BARREL CEO JULIE MASINO TO STEP DOWN

The controversial attempt to modernize resulted in Cracker Barrel being compared to other brands that have irked conservatives in recent memory, such as Bud Light and Target. 

The company reversed course amid widespread outrage, with Masino explaining that the effort missed the mark and stemmed from an effort to improve the guest experience at its locations.

Cracker Barrel shared a social media post that included a 32-second video of the "Old Timer" sign being restored and the decorations on the wall inside one of its remodeled restaurants being removed.

The ordeal generated so much attention that President Donald Trump even chimed in, first urging Cracker Barrel on social media to bring back the original logo and then congratulating the restaurant for listening. 

CRACKER BARREL SALES, TRAFFIC CONTINUE TO SLUMP MONTHS AFTER FAILED REBRAND

Less than a year after the about-face, Masino is set to exit the company. She will remain with Cracker Barrel in an advisory capacity until Oct. 9. David Deno has been named as her replacement. 

Cracker Barrel's announcement of the leadership turnover also included a statement from Deno, who said the chain is a "truly iconic American brand, defined by its unique combination of warm country hospitality, timeless appeal, and deep connection with guests across generations."

Kohberger plans to argue that he had bad counsel. Court records show he filed a petition for post-conviction relief Monday, but the filing itself was not immediately available.

The New York Times was first to report this story after Kohberger called a reporter directly and claimed that he has an "absolute claim of innocence" in his first public remarks outside the courtroom.

IDAHO MURDERS EVIDENCE LEAK TRIGGERS CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION FOR INSIDER WHO SPILLED SECRETS: REPORT

"My actual innocence is my truth, and the plea, hinged on by false promises and blatant disinformation, MUST be withdrawn," he told the outlet.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

item.title: Trump demands Thune keep Senate in session until SAVE America Act passes
item.description: Trump demands John Thune cancel Senate recess until the SAVE America Act passes, renewing his call to terminate the filibuster for GOP priorities.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump doesn’t want the Senate to leave town with his flagship election security measure still on the line.

It’s less than two weeks until the upper chamber makes a jailbreak from Washington, D.C., and the schedule is already jam-packed with key items, from blockbuster confirmations to a long-awaited sanctions package targeting Russia.

But only one legislative priority matters to Trump: the SAVE America Act. And despite the political reality in the Senate, the president wants the bill passed by any means necessary.

TRUMP'S SAVE AMERICA ACT STALLS AS MCCONNELL'S ABSENCE COMPLICATES SENATE PATH

"John Thune should not allow the United States Senate to ‘leave town’ until it passes The Save America Act or, far better still, TERMINATES THE FILIBUSTER, where Republicans can then quickly pass everything they ever dreamed of, including a full and deep-throated SAVE AMERICA ACT, the Budget, and the ever looming Debt Ceiling disaster, 1929," Trump declared on Truth Social.

"The Dumocrats will do it on day one and can’t believe how lucky they got with this Senate leadership," he continued. "Remember, stupidity always brings LOSING & DEATH!"

GOP RIFT GROWS AS THUNE HITS BRAKES ON TRUMP'S ELECTION BILL TO AVERT SHUTDOWN

While Congress’ annual break during August is often viewed outside the Beltway as vacation time for lawmakers, during a midterm election year, it allows for crucial hours on the road for incumbents to have face time with voters and make their pitch to keep their seat.

Republicans are hungry to campaign and sell their agenda, particularly last year’s tax cut package, Trump’s "one big, beautiful bill," but are facing headwinds from the war in Iran and affordability issues.

And there are three races on the 2026 map that are troubling for the Senate GOP in its quest to maintain its majority: Maine, Alaska and Ohio.

Still, Trump has warned that unless the Senate passes the SAVE America Act, they will suffer the consequences at the ballot box, and he has routinely called for the elimination of the filibuster for many of his priorities, but neither has the votes to happen in the upper chamber.

TRUMP'S PATIENCE 'RUNNING OUT' AS THUNE FIRES BACK OVER STALLED ELECTION SECURITY BILL

It comes as tensions between the White House and Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., are on the rise.

Last week, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt warned that Trump’s patience was "running out" with Thune over the legislation, which prompted the top Senate Republican to fire back that the White House should focus its energy on Democrats blocking the SAVE America Act and work the phones to get Republicans to a "yes" vote.

Trump is also not alone in his push for Thune to cancel the upcoming break.

Sens. Mike Lee, R-Utah, Rick Scott, R-Fla., and Ashley Moody, R-Fla., have all announced their intent online to object to Thune calling for recess toward the end of this work period.

"I hereby object to any effort to put the Senate into recess in August — at least until such time as the Senate has passed the SAVE America Act — and hereby request a roll call vote," Lee said on X.

"Do not assume you have my consent," he continued. "You do not."

Typically, recess or state work periods are a consent exercise in the Senate, meaning that all lawmakers agree to skip town and head back to their states to do work on the ground. But a single senator can object on the Senate floor and force a vote to decide whether the upper chamber stays or goes.

Trump and the GOP trio’s demands come at an inflection point in the Senate.

Thune has prioritized averting a government shutdown and is encouraging ongoing negotiations between Republicans and Democrats to hammer out a deal before the break begins. He’s threatened to hold the House-passed budget resolution that would, among other things, set up a rough framework to pass the SAVE America Act through budget reconciliation.

All that comes after he and other Republicans have made clear the political reality that the SAVE America Act, as written, does not have the votes to pass in the upper chamber, neither from Democrats nor the GOP.

And whether the legislation, or a version of it, can survive the reconciliation process remains to be seen, given that, as written, the SAVE America Act is primarily policy and doesn’t have a budgetary impact — a key requirement of the party line process.

"It's still likely to be a 60-vote exercise, even if it's done with a budget resolution," Thune told Fox News Digital. "Unless it's done with, you know, structured to allow grants to states that’s incentive-based, and principally budgetary, not policy."

item.title: FIFA president's leaked letter to Argentina following World Cup Final brawl comes across as tone deaf

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 World Cup was a smashing success, but that doesn't mean certain aspects of the event should be off limits to criticism, and that's especially true when it comes to a recently leaked letter from FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

Following Spain's extra-time win over Argentina in the World Cup Final, several different on-field brawls broke out between players and team staff members. Argentina's Leandro Paredes caught the most attention after appearing to grab Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat, which set off more back-and-forths around the pitch.

Infantino either forgot that several Argentina members were involved in the on-field brawl, or is simply choosing to ignore that fact.

SPAIN COACH DE LA FUENTE SAYS ARGENTINA WORLD CUP FINAL CONDUCT 'UNACCEPTABLE'

The FIFA president reportedly sent a letter to Argentine Federation president Claudio Tapia. The letter, which was leaked in Argentina and subsequently verified by the Daily Mail, highlighted Argentina's "professionalism."

"I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine soccer," the letter reportedly began.

"The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world," the letter reportedly continued.

"Please send my sincere congratulations to all who have contributed to this magnificent result: to the players, to coach Lionel Scaloni, as well as to the coaching and medical staff and, of course, to the many fans who have accompanied and encouraged the team throughout the competition.

"These victories are always the fruit of constant work, professionalism and attention to detail, but also of passion, commitment and love for this wonderful sport. All this augurs a very promising future and, without a doubt, will pave the way for new and great successes for Argentine football."

Perhaps the most shocking piece in all of this is that FIFA launched an official investigation into the altercations that broke out following the final whistle of the final.

So, the on-field brawls were aggressive enough to launch an investigation, but not so aggressive that congratulatory letters were off limits?

At the time of this writing, FIFA's investigation into the on-field brawls following the final whistle is still ongoing.

item.title: GIANNO CALDWELL: We marched for every family blue city politicians left behind
item.description: The march drew crowds near where the author's brother was murdered, but Gov. JB Pritzker and Mayor Brandon Johnson never responded to invitations.
item.content:encoded:
This weekend I marched through the streets of Chicago, a few blocks from where my innocent teenage brother Christian was murdered four years ago.

That loss is what led me to found the Caldwell Foundation for Public Safety, driven by one belief: that no family should ever have to go through what mine did. Community members lined the sidewalks and cheered as we passed. That moment told me everything I needed to know about who is truly fighting for these communities and who isn't.

I invited Illinois Governor JB Pritzker and Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson to join us. I called their offices. I emailed them. I listed the invitation in my Fox News op-ed. I extended the invitation publicly on national and local television multiple times. They never responded. Not once. Not a word. Not an acknowledgment. Two of the most powerful elected officials in Illinois could not even extend the basic courtesy of a response to the families of murder victims gathering in their own city.

GIANNO CALDWELL: FOUR YEARS AFTER MY BROTHER’S MURDER, I’M MARCHING FOR JUSTICE

Let that settle in. The governor of Illinois and the mayor of Chicago took an oath to serve the people of this state and this city. They had no answer for the mothers who have buried their children. No answer for the fathers who live with a hole in their hearts that never heals. No answer for the communities that have been failed by the same political machine for decades. They chose not to respond. Again and again.

Their silence was loud. And the community noticed.

This is what failed leadership looks like in real time. Chicago was once one of the great economic engines of the Midwest. Today it is a cautionary tale. Ken Griffin, one of the most successful investors in American history, lived in Chicago for more than 30 years before packing up Citadel and 900 employees and moving to Miami. He did not leave quietly. "I had two colleagues who had bullets fly through their cars," Griffin told Fox News. "I had 25 bullet holes in the front of my building where I lived. You can't live in a city awash in violent crime." Illinois has lost a net 1.6 million people to domestic outmigration since 2000, and Chicago's population is at its lowest level in nearly a century. The families who cannot afford to leave are the ones paying the price for every bad policy decision made by the people who were supposed to protect them. And in some cases, they are paying with their lives.

NORTH TEXAS DOMINATES IN POPULATION GROWTH AS BIG BLUE CITIES FAIL TO RECOVER TO PRE-PANDEMIC LEVELS

Nearly 7,000 people have been murdered in Chicago over the last decade. Seven thousand. They are sons and daughters. Brothers and sisters. Friends and neighbors. People who deserved to grow old, to raise families, to build something with their lives. Darren Bailey, the Republican nominee challenging Governor Pritzker, captured the purpose of the march when he said: "People in Chicago shouldn't be living under a death sentence, and that's essentially what's taking place right now. Gianno's brother Christian should be here today, and this summer, and at this school, and he's not." He is right. Christian should be here. So should every victim taken from this city over the last decade. Bob Fioretti, the Republican candidate for Illinois Attorney General, put the current toll in stark terms: "So far in the city of Chicago this year, over 1,000 people have been shot. 220 of them have been killed. Last night alone in our city, there was one killed, six wounded. This is unacceptable."

Among those who spoke at the march was Apostle Anthony Wilson, a man of God and a grieving father who stood before the crowd and shared the story of his daughter Alicia Prince, murdered just two months ago. "No one should have to bury their child before their time," he said, pausing to collect himself before the crowd. Two months. Her family is still in shock, thrust into a reality too many families know all too well. Apostle Wilson's presence embodied everything this march was about. Not politics. Not party. A father demanding that his daughter's life meant something. That it must mean something.

Christian Maxwell, who is running for Congress in Illinois's 1st Congressional District, spoke to the heart of what is at stake for these communities. "Safety is not partisan," she said. "We want to fight for children to be able to ride their bikes and walk to school safely. That is not a hard thing to achieve when leaders are focused on the right outcome."

CHICAGO PASTOR GATHERS HUNDREDS OF MEN TO DECLARE VIOLENCE-FREE ZONE ON SOUTH SIDE

Christine McGovern, who is running for Illinois State Senate in the district where we marched, spoke to something that too many people are afraid to say out loud. "They are so desensitized to what has happened," she said. "We cannot normalize the death of our kids on the streets."

These were just a few of the many voices who showed up to be heard.

As I led the march through the streets of Chicago, I called out what these communities have been saying for years but have not had a platform to say loud enough. We demand safe streets. Enough is enough. Save our streets. The crowd echoed every word. Because they have lived it. Because they are tired of burying people they love while elected officials offer nothing but excuses.

National and local media were there because this story can no longer be ignored.

We started at Morgan Park High School, where Christian walked the halls before his life was stolen. As we marched through the streets of Chicago, I thought about what it means to return to the place where everything changed. The pain never goes away. But this weekend it was joined by something else. Hope. Because when you see a community come out and cheer for a march against the very violence that has devastated them, you understand that the people have not given up. They are not waiting to be saved. They are demanding to be heard. And it is past time for those in power to listen.

That leadership did not come from the governor's mansion this weekend. It did not come from City Hall. It came from the people who showed up, who linked arms, who said with their feet and their presence that they refuse to accept this as normal.

The Caldwell Foundation for Public Safety is not stopping here. We will continue to march in every city, in every state where our presence is needed most. The pain of losing a child to violence knows no zip code. Neither does our commitment to stopping it.

Governor Pritzker. Mayor Johnson. You had your chance to stand with these families. You chose not to, again and again. The people of Chicago are watching. And they deserve leaders who show up, not just at election time, but when it matters most.

item.title: States may defy DNC primary calendar as 'nobody is scared' of Ken Martin, CNN reporter says
item.description: CNN's Edward Isaac-Dovere said states like New Hampshire could defy the DNC primary calendar because "nobody" is scared of Ken Martin as chair.
item.content:encoded:
CNN's Edward Isaac-Dovere suggested Sunday that states could buck the DNC's primary schedule and hold its elections whenever they want to, pointing to New Hampshire specifically, and said that "nobody" is scared of DNC Chair Ken Martin.

"There is the possibility that a state could choose to not follow the DNC here and hold its primary when they want to," Dovere said as CNN host Manu Raju added that New Hampshire wanted to do this.

"And people saying, 'Hey, the DNC is broke. They can't do anything to help us anyway. Nobody is scared in any way of Ken Martin as the chair. And so maybe they'll just go and violate it.' It is not where the infrastructure of the party needs to be for going into 2026 and then 2028," Dovere added.

The DNC Rules and Bylaws Committee (RBC) panel, meeting in the nation's capital on Friday, picked South Carolina over Nevada to hold the party's first presidential nominating contest in 2028, a move that will likely maintain a key role in the primary calendar for Black voters, who are a crucial part of the Democrats' base.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

The decision came after intense lobbying by both states, and by New Hampshire and Iowa over the past year to hold the much-coveted lead-off Democratic primary in the race for the White House. 

The battle between South Carolina and Nevada was seen as a struggle between rewarding Black voters and outreach to Latino voters, with whom President Donald Trump and Republicans made major gains in the 2024 election, handing Democrats major setbacks.

The New Hampshire Democratic Party pointed Fox News Digital to a statement they put out on Friday, in which New Hampshire Democratic Party chair Ray Buckley said that the national party didn't learn anything from 2024.

"Today’s vote shows that many party insiders have learned nothing from 2024. New Hampshire has a proven track record of testing our candidates with a rigorous, fair, and efficient process, yet those qualities did not prevail. This committee’s vote does not change the realities governing New Hampshire’s primary, which are beyond the control of both this committee and our state party," Buckley said.

Buckley continued, "Democrats’ guiding North Star should be winning general elections, and New Hampshire Democrats will get back to work focusing on the 2026 elections and addressing the significant challenges facing America’s overwhelmed working class. Today’s vote moves the party further away from that objective."

SLOTKIN SAYS DEMOCRATIC PARTY NEEDS 'NEW LEADERSHIP': 'OLD MODELS ARE NO LONGER WORKING'

Raju asked if Martin would "survive" as chairman. Dovere said that the DNC chair could only be kicked out of the position if he resigned.

"He cannot be kicked out, and so it's up to him," he added. 

The DNC pointed Fox News Digital to a press release from June that highlighted the RBC's vote to strengthen penalties for states and candidates that buck the calendar.

The DNC voted at the end of June to strengthen penalties for states who participate in an unsanctioned contest in the early window of the presidential nominating calendar, according to a press release from late June.

The rules include implementing a $270,000 fine for any state that hosts an unsanctioned contest and increasing the delegates lost for states that host an unsanctioned contest from 50% to 100%, including all automatic delegates, among others. The penalties also prohibit any candidate's participation in DNC debates if they violate the early window rules.

DNC CHAIR KEN MARTIN THREW PHONE AT AIDE'S DESK, FACED HR COMPLAINT IN SIGN OF 'FRAYING NERVES': REPORT

Martin, while speaking to reporters on Friday, was asked how the DNC would respond, should states such as New Hampshire go rogue.

"We have put in significant penalties and sanctions, probably the most enforcement mechanisms ever, to make sure that, you know, folks know we are serious about making sure the calendar we put forth is abided by. Not just by the parties themselves – the state parties – but by also by the candidates," Martin told reporters.

He added, "If there’s a consequence to the candidates, right, the candidates are going to have to decide whether or not they want to lose all their delegates in the first four states. Whether they want to lose access to the debate stage. I can’t imagine if one of those states moves into the early window and is not sanctioned, that presidential candidates are going to risk it, risk going there."

New Hampshire state law requires that the state hold its primary election at least seven days before any other state holds a "similar" election.

When South Carolina was selected as the first primary state in 2024, New Hampshire defied the DNC, and former President Joe Biden left his name off the ballot, though he still won the state as a write-in.

While the DNC threatened to withhold New Hampshire's delegates in an effort to get the state to comply, they were ultimately restored in April 2024, ending the feud between the DNC and New Hampshire's Democratic Party in the previous presidential election cycle, according to the AP.

Martin faced a formal human resources complaint after allegedly throwing his phone at a junior aide's desk at the party's Washington headquarters in early July, The New York Times reported Sunday.

The Times cited six people familiar with the incident, none of whom witnessed it firsthand. Their accounts differed over how forcefully Martin threw the phone, but the newspaper reported that it landed on the aide's desk while Martin was reprimanding the staffer and led to a formal HR complaint.

NOTUS also reported on DNC turmoil on Sunday, noting a source briefed on the episode described it as worsening conduct.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"It's just f---ing unacceptable. This is spiraling behavior," the source told NOTUS.

The RNC blasted the national Democratic Party operation in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"The DNC is broke, leaderless, and imploding before America’s eyes. From states defying the national party to Ken Martin throwing his phone at staffers, it is undeniable that the inmates are running the asylum. While the Democrat Party collapses, Republicans are united, on offense, and focused on electing our candidates up and down the ballot this November," RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre said in a statement.

item.content:encoded:

CALLING 911 BECAUSE A BAR WON’T SERVE YOU A JELL-O SHOT IS WHAT POLICE REFER TO AS A MISUSE OF SERVICES
